# The tools (generated by `python -I tools/toolindex.py` from each tool's docstring: edit the docstring, not this file)

Shared rules are in `.claude/skills/elin-play/SKILL.md` (the thresholds, the hard rules); what each tool's domain taught us is in
`knowledge/tool-notes.md`. Every tool: exit 0 done, 1 refused, 2 the bridge, 3 stopped for a decision.

- **`ability.py`**: Use an ability by its name from the ability window (Start Run 1): Rest, Pray. Opens the window, right-clicks the button with that name in the same step as listing it, and closes the window, so nothing else can shift the list in between.
    usage: python -I tools/ability.py NAME        e.g. python -I tools/ability.py Rest
    Exit 0 used, 1 refused (no such ability), 2 the bridge.
- **`act.py`**: Perform the act at a cell whose text starts with TEXT (case-insensitive), never by index: a creature standing on the cell puts its own acts (Talk, Attack...) first (run 03: `do 0` meant to read a letter opened Kaberg's dialog instead).
    usage: python -I tools/act.py DX DZ TEXT [mode]     e.g. act.py -1 0 Read
           python -I tools/act.py find NAME TEXT [mode]  the nearest thing/object NAME, e.g.
                                                         act.py find package Open
    mode: all (default) | left | key | right
- **`activity.py`**: Mark the start and end of a timed activity for the run tracker (the review of 2026-10-23: the owner's measure is growth per real hour, and no log said what each activity earned). Each mark is one row in runs/activity.csv: the real clock, the game date, the tag, the phase, exp, level, gold, gold bars, the zone. stats.py pairs a start with its end and derives exp and orens per real hour per tag; the loops call it themselves, so the numbers need no hand work at the close-out.
    usage: python -I tools/activity.py TAG start|end [NOTE]
- **`arena.py`**: Clear a job's arena instance ("Monster's Den": Monster extermination, Monster hunting, Troubled home) to "You have wiped out the nearby monsters!" (Start Run 2: hunt.py stops at 70% HP and walks toward the edge, where "Leave Monster's Den?" would forfeit the job). Loop: fight the nearest foe, Rest when nothing is in view and HP is under 70%, else walk the map's corners and middle. Ends at the wipe, then loots, leaves and picks up the reward.
    usage: python -I tools/arena.py [--no-leave] [--any] [--wiped]   --wiped: already wiped, only loot, leave and pick the reward
    Exit 0 wiped (and left), 1 refused (not in an arena), 3 stopped.
- **`arrive.py`**: Arrive home (run 19, the user's rule after run 18): the scripted part of elin-home section 1, in order, with the Dishes box shared first. leave.py made it private on the way out (dishes.py).
    usage: python -I tools/arrive.py
    Exit: 0 done, 1 refused (not at home), 3 stopped (a threat, or the Dishes box couldn't be shared).
- **`audit.py`**: Tally every home container by kind (G70 Smart Storage M1, run 57; the user, 2026-11-21: "go carefully through our current storage rules, what we currently have available, and make some decisions about what we need to keep and what we need to sell"). Reads the bridge's `stock` op once (every installed container on the home map, without walking), sorts each stack by the game's own category (things.json, never a word in its name: elin-play's rule since runs 47-50), and counts how many of the game's recipes take each thing, by its id or its category (graph.json's `needs` edges, kb.py's source).
    usage: python -I tools/audit.py [--csv PATH] [--top N]
      prints one block per category, largest first: stacks, items, the containers holding it, the recipes that use it, and its
      N biggest kinds (default 6); --csv writes one row per kind (category, id, name, stacks, items, recipe uses, containers).
    Exit 0, 2 the bridge.
- **`bag.py`**: Move items between the pack and a container carried in it (Cooler Box, purse, bag) with the game's own Shift+click quick move (bridge 0.13.0 `shiftclick`, InvOwner.OnShiftClick). A carried container holds many items in one pack slot (the user, run 04: carry bags so the pack stops overflowing; keep food in the cooler box).
    usage: python -I tools/bag.py BAG [--take] [ITEM ...]
      BAG     part of the container's name ("Cooler Box"), or uid:N (tools/items.py)
      ITEM    part of an item's name, or uid:N; each moves one stack
      --take  move from the bag to the pack (to eat or use it)
      no ITEM lists what the bag holds
    Exit: 0 every item moved, 1 any item not moved (run 38: a full pack exited 0).
    item.py finds items inside an open bag too (run 04: `item.py "piles of bread" Eat` ate from the Cooler Box); --take raised a NullReference in the game on the world map.
- **`blanket.py`**: Fireproof blankets from the home's own stock (G65, run 54; the user: "a Goal on how to keep Fireproof Blankets in stock (either through stores or creation, it's clearly a frequent issue)"). Runs 42-53 left home on 0-1 blankets with 160 waivers in 12 days while 145 skins and 55 hide fibers sat in the boxes: the minimum counted only finished textures.
    usage: python -I tools/blanket.py [--target N=6] [--max N] [--floor SP=40] [--dry]
      --target  charged fireproof blankets wanted across the pack and the home boxes; makes the difference
      --max     at most N this call
      --floor   SP left at the end, at least (the trip after; no stage starts that would cross it)
      --dry     print the stock, the plan and its SP, and act on nothing
    Exit 0 made (or none needed), 1 refused, 2 the bridge, 3 stopped (a hostile, a window, a stage short of SP or stock).
- **`board.py`**: List a town's jobs from its nearest quest board in one step (Start Run 1: town jobs were a new character's best income: 247 orens and +1 influence in 3 real minutes). Walks next to the nearest ordinary board, opens it and prints each job with its reward, danger and time. The board stays open, so a job is `bridge.py click N expect=NAME` from the list. All boards in a town show the same jobs.
    usage: python -I tools/board.py [--close]
           python -I tools/board.py --take NAME [NAME ...]   accept these jobs in order, each by its name on the board (an instance job moves
                                                             me into it as its dialog ends, so it goes last); under Lv15 it refuses an instance
                                                             job below Lv4 or without the ally beside me at 70%+ (--weak-ok)
    Exit 0 listed, 1 refused (no board known on this map), 2 the bridge.
- **`box.py`**: Open a container, move named items into it (or out of it with --take), close it. With no items, list what it holds. One process and one bridge connection: calling item.py from a script that holds the bridge blocks it (the bridge serves one client at a time; run 04).
    usage: python -I tools/box.py WHERE [--take] [ITEM ...]
      WHERE  X,Z of the container, or its name ("shipping chest", "shared sturdy box")
      ITEM   part of the item's name, e.g. "granite stone" "7 burnable" (one stack per ITEM)
      e.g.   python -I tools/box.py "shipping chest" "straw shirt" "empty bottle"
             python -I tools/box.py 53,53 --take "granite pickaxe"
    Storage rule (Props.ListThingStack): at home a station draws ingredients from the pack and
    every installed container on the map, at any distance, but one stack per recipe slot. So
    keep each crafting material in a single stack, in one box.
- **`boxcount.py`**: Count every home container by hand (G54 M0, the user 2026-11-08: "you may need to hand count the boxes and do a full sweep to check inventory"): the bridge's stock op reports a ★Storage Chest as 96 slots whatever its wrenches (fact #1014), but the open container window shows "USED / SIZE" (run 45: the yard chest 68,44 read 199 / 280). So this walks to each installed container the stock op lists, opens it, reads that line, closes it, and writes one row per container with the stock op's contents by kind.
    usage: python -I tools/boxcount.py [--run NN] [--walk-all] [X,Z ...]
      Walks only the ★Storage Chests (the one kind whose window has the line); --walk-all opens every container (run 45's
      sweep: 72 opened, three locked: the practice chest, Fiama's quest chest, a boss chest at 65,40).
      writes runs/boxcount-NN.csv (x, z, name, used, size, by_stock_op, top contents) and prints the totals:
      containers, real slots, used, free; and the small ones (size 24 or less) with what they hold.
    Every step runs farmday.home_guard first (run 41: a box walk with no stops ended in two deaths).
    Exit 0 counted, 2 the bridge, 3 stopped (home_guard, a container that wouldn't open).
- **`boxshift.py`**: Move a box that holds things (G12, run 18): a filled container can't be grabbed ("You can't put that in your backpack!"), so empty it into a carried bag with the game's Shift+click (with the box and the bag open, a box stack goes into the bag), grab the empty box, place it, open it there and Shift+click the same stacks back. The box keeps its own name, sharing and priority settings.
    usage: python -I tools/boxshift.py FX,FZ TX,TZ [--bag "loot bag"]
           python -I tools/boxshift.py FX,FZ TX,TZ --contents   only the contents, into the box already
                  at TX,TZ, in trips that never pass Heavy Burden (run 18: a parts box of scrap and cans
                  in one bag left me Squashed, 125 -> 101 HP); the emptied box stays where it was
    The bag must have room for the box's stacks (the loot bag holds 35); stops (exit 3) if a stack
    won't move, leaving everything where it is now (box, bag or pack) and saying so.
    After a move, update tools/home.py and the elin-home table.
- **`bridge.py`**: Client for the ElinBridge mod (127.0.0.1:47323). One JSON line out, one back.
    usage: python -I tools/bridge.py <op> [args]
      ping                      bridge version and frame counter
      state                     player, zone, visible creatures, message log, open layers, dialog
      buttons [--all] [text=T] [name=N] [card=C]
                                clickable buttons in the top UI layer (or everywhere); the filters
                                are substrings and keep the full listing's indices (0.23.0)
      closetop                  close the top UI layer as its own close button does
      shiftclick N              the game's quick move of inventory slot N into the open container
      drag I J [N]              drag slot I onto slot J (a hotbar slot, a picker's ing1, a crafter)
      altitude [D]              the placement height for the next Place (wall-mounted items)
      qcraft                    the floating Quick Craft list (the game's altCraft option): each recipe, its skill,
                                and the thing each ingredient would take (0.41.0, run 47)
      qcraftdo id=RECIPE|i=N    start one craft from that list as a click on its slot does (guarded; 0.41.0)
      speed [1|2|3]             the game's own speed control (a hotbar's changeSpeed shortcut): x1, x2, x5; no index reads it (0.38.0)
      places [R]                world map: known places within R with distance and danger
      power                     my attacks, defense and resists as the game computes them
      actions                   every EAction name the input layer knows
      boxcfg [priority=N] [allow=food,weapon|all] [norotten=1] ["name=X"] [bag=CARRIED]
                                an open container's distribution settings (shared-box routing)
      cells DX,DZ ...           several `cell` reads in one call (0.23.0)
      wait [until=idle|zone|layer|moved|frames] [n=N] [timeout=MS]
                                the reply comes when the condition holds (ok, done=true) or at the
                                timeout (done=false): no sleep-and-poll loops (0.23.0)
      walkto X Z [r=4] [hp=60] [timeout=MS] [stairs=1] [weakok=1]
                                goto with the reply on arrival, or when the walk stops short, a
                                hostile comes within r (the walk is cancelled), HP falls under hp%,
                                a window opens or the zone changes; a stairway target needs stairs=1
      texts [--all] [--full]    visible text in the top UI layer (or everywhere); --full: no
                                200-character cut (letters, books)
      cancel                    stop my running task (training, fishing) as a click/Wait does
      find NAME [R] [N]         things, objects and visible creatures by name on the explored map
      sources [TABLE [OFF [N]]] the game's data tables (no TABLE: names and sizes); kb.py uses it
      click N [expect=T]        click button N from the last `buttons` listing; with expect=, refused
                                unless button N's text (or card) still contains T (0.25.0: any tool's
                                `buttons` call replaces the listing, run 14's Policy tab)
      rclick N [expect=T]       right-click button N (abilities: use); `buttons` marks these [R]
      hover N                   show button N's tooltip as a mouse hover would; then `tip`
      tip                       the text of the tooltip(s) on screen
      cell DX DZ                what an explored cell holds: floor, wall, object, things; the floor's and
                                block's material, hardness and reqHarvest (0.31.0)
      skills                    every skill on the sheet with its level (0.31.0)
      witness [R]               who could witness a hostile act (mining in a town): the creatures I see
                                within R (default 6) and the cells in line of sight I can't see (0.31.0)
      choose N                  pick dialog choice N
      act ACTION [frames]       inject a game action: Wait Interact Search Pick Fire Use Confirm
                                Cancel MenuInventory MenuChara MenuJournal MenuAbility GetAll ...
      move DIR [frames]         step by SCREEN direction: n s e w ne nw se sw
      step DX DZ                step by MAP delta (each -1..1); +x = screen SE, +z = screen NE
      goto X Z                  auto-walk to an explored map cell (the game's own pathing)
      map [R]                   ASCII map of explored cells within R (default 8)
      inv                       the player's inventory (top level)
      terrain [R] [WANT] [N]    world map: tile counts by biome/alias within R, and the N nearest
                                tiles matching WANT ("beach", "Sand", "Forest") with road distance and
                                the danger a field there gets (0.20.0)
      acts DX DZ [all|left|key] the game's own action list for the cell at map delta DX,DZ, as
                                the context menu (all, default), a left click or a keypress sees it
      do N                      perform act N from the last `acts` (as the context menu does)
                                mode `right` lists what the held item / hotbar tool does there
      invacts N                 right-click menu of inventory slot N (open the inventory with
                                `act MenuInventory`, then `buttons`; slots show [item name])
      invdo K                   perform entry K of the last `invacts`
      winbtn [NAME]             an open inventory window's header buttons (shown only on hover):
                                no NAME lists them; buttonShared toggles a container's share lock
      anykey                    "press any key" (intros, waits)
      load ID                   from the title screen, load the LOCAL save ID (e.g. world_2).
                                Never loads a cloud save and never changes the cloud setting.
      autocombat UID            fight that creature through the game's own auto-combat (0.26.0):
                                a lethal hit on anyone healthy at its start leaves them at 0 HP once
      abortcombat               stop the auto-combat
      quit                      save, then exit Elin through the game's own Quit (refuses if the
                                save fails). Runs only under the user's allow rule (see CLAUDE.md).
    Exit code 1 when the bridge answers ok=false, 2 when it is not reachable.
    World ops (goto, move, step, do, walkto) are refused by the bridge while a dialog or pop-up is
    open ("window open: LayerX"); read it with talk.py, or read.py then close.py.
- **`butcher.py`**: Butcher every corpse in the pack and the Cooler Box with the butcher's tool (run 13, G6).
    usage: python -I tools/butcher.py [--dry] [NAME ...]   (NAME: only corpses matching these words)
- **`buyfood.py`**: Turn gold into food at an open or named shop in one step (Start Run 3: five inn visits of hand-reading tooltips in two hours): sell every old ticket, read each food's nutrition from its tooltip, and buy by food per oren until the budget is gone. Meals earlyday.py doesn't know yet go in runs/foods.txt, one word a line, for it to eat.
    usage: python -I tools/buyfood.py [--keep N] [--shop ROLE_ID] [--min-ratio R=0.55]   stand by the shopkeeper (default merchant_inn); N orens are kept
      --min-ratio R  skip food under R nutrition an oren (0 buys every dish: a stock-up for a long stay)
    Exit 0 done, 1 refused (no shopkeeper near).
- **`cast.py`**: Cast an attack spell at a hostile from range (bridge 0.33.0 `cast`: the game's own ButtonAbility.TryUse path, pc.UseAbility then EndTurn, with every rule of the game kept: range, line of sight, the spell stock, cooldowns). Run 27's 『Kobold』 (23% a round in melee, PV-heavy) had no ranged answer, and the stocked attack spells were barely cast (the user's tip after run 27). Each cast trains Casting by twice the MP spent (Chara.UseAbility: elements.ModExp(304, MP x 2)), and only a Casting level-up pays character exp: a weak exp engine at 69 MP, a free ranged attack all the same.
    usage: python -I tools/cast.py [SPELL=arrow_Cold] [NAME] [CASTS=10] [--mp-floor N] [--hp N] [--until PCT]
      --until PCT  (run 29, G20's monster ball) stop once the target is at or under PCT% HP (exit 0), or when the
                   biggest drop a cast round has made could kill it from where it stands (exit 3)
      SPELL  the ability's alias (power.py lists them with their stock: arrow_Cold, arrow_Nerve, bolt_Fire)
      NAME   a word of the target's name (whole words); default the nearest hostile
    Exit 0 the target died (or none left), 1 refused (no such spell, the bridge refused the cast),
    3 stopped (MP at the floor, HP under the floor, a window, the target out of sight).
- **`chests.py`**: Empty every mystic treasure chest in the pack at home and ship the empty chest (run 41: Poppy's Treasure Hunt leaves them on the floor for arrive.py to pick up, digmap.py brings them home; packcheck had no rule for them, and each held up a home trip, G46). Everything inside comes out to the pack, the medals and bars go through packcheck --move; a chest is worth ~112-200 shipped (elin-pack). Close each chest before the next: an open one takes every later quick move (run 25).
    usage: python -I tools/chests.py [--dry]
           python -I tools/chests.py --field   on a trip (run 41: five chests on a dig tour, 15 weight each, Burden phase 2): the money, medals,
                                               unidentified pieces and books go into the pack and bags, the chest stays on the tile with the rest
    Exit 0 done (or none), 1 refused (not at home), 3 stopped (the pack full: a chest left as it is).
- **`circuit.py`**: The nefia circuit as one loop (the review of 2026-10-30, the user's ok): run 30's 820 points an hour was this done by hand. From the world map: `places` -> the nearest unconquered nefia of base danger LO-HI within R tiles (no underwater ones) -> wgo.py there -> Enter -> ladder.py (the gate, FLOORS floors) -> on "conquered" evac.py out -> repeat, until N nefias, or a ladder stop that isn't a conquest, or the unload is due.
    usage: python -I tools/circuit.py [N=4] [--danger LO-HI=3-7] [--r 15] [--floors 5] [--unattended] [--solo] [--wrecks] [--danger-ok N] [--skip NAME ...] [--blanket-ok 'why']
      --blanket-ok 'why'  passed to each ladder: a nefia with no charged blanket, a row in runs/waivers.csv each time (the user, 2026-11-06)
      --wrecks  mine the wrecks on each floor (ladder.py without --no-wrecks; run 34, G35: iron wrecks drop a battery and a
                microchip each, the Gene Machine's power parts)
      --danger-ok N  passed to wgo.py: a deliberate crossing of ambush levels up to N (elin-play's route rule)
      --skip NAME    leave out a nefia whose name contains NAME (repeatable): one whose master lies below the gate
      --until HH:MM  no new nefia after this clock time (run 42: the shipping and the close-out wait on the circuit; a nefia is ~10 real minutes)
    It registers as a job (runs/jobs/circuit.json: journal.py refuses while it runs) and runs/jobs/circuit.stop ends it between nefias.
    Started on a nefia's floor it runs the ladder there first (run 40). A nefia that expires before the walk and a conquest is skipped,
    and a nap at the door happens only when the nefia outlives it (run 48, bridge 0.42.0 expireH). An empty list gets one nap to refill it (run 40).
    Exit 0 after N conquests, 1 refused (not on the world map or a nefia, the kit), 3 stopped (a ladder decision, no nefia
    in range, the unload due).
- **`clear.py`**: Clear wild plants off the home map to bring the soil back under its limit (G3, run 05).
    usage: python -I tools/clear.py OBJECT [N=20] [min_sp=8] [radius=60] [--tool NAME] [--skip X0,Z0,X1,Z1]
      e.g. python -I tools/clear.py "white flower" 30 --tool "woodcutter's axe"
    --tool holds that pack item first. --skip leaves a box alone (the field: mushrooms are planted
    there too, run 10). Only objects inside the zone's bounds are taken (run 10: the map holds ten
    times more plants outside them, and they cost no soil), unripe fruit plants included. Any held tool speeds plant work by its material's hardness
    (BaseTaskHarvest: toolLv += hardness; run 05: iron axe 5 flowers in 13 game minutes, bare hands
    9 minutes for one). Only the soil inside zone.bounds counts; plants outside it are "edge".
    Harvests up to N objects named OBJECT, nearest first, skipping the map edge (only "Enter" there)
    and anything that gives no harvest act. Stops at the SP floor, on a hostile or a window.
    Drops are picked up; food goes to the Cooler Box afterwards by hand (bag.py).
- **`clearout.py`**: The clear-out of home storage by the keep rules (G70 Smart Storage M4, run 57): every stack keep.py calls "sell" or "trash" is taken from its box into the pack's own grid, a batch at a time, then sold to the home shopkeeper (sell.py, the resident board's Find walks me to her) or dropped in the trash can (trash.py dump). The approved calls are in knowledge/storage-audit.md (the user, 2026-11-21); gear ("gear") waits for gearcheck.py, unidentified things for Aliyun.
    usage: python -I tools/clearout.py [--calls sell,trash] [--batches N] [--buyer NAME] [--chest] [--dry]
      --calls    which of keep.py's calls to clear (default sell,trash)
      --batches  stop after N batches (default 99)
      --buyer    the shopkeeper (default "Samata": the name talkto sees)
      --chest    the "sell" stacks go to the shipping chest instead of the shopkeeper (when her shop won't take more)
      --dry      print the plan (boxes and stacks per call) and move nothing
      To end a run between batches: create runs/jobs/clearout.stop (it is removed when read).
    Exit 0 done (nothing left, or N batches), 1 refused (the grid has no room), 3 stopped (home_guard, a take or sale failed,
    the buyer out of money).
- **`close.py`**: Close the top window safely, the right way for its type, and never leave the System menu open. A blind `act Cancel` is dangerous: when nothing (or only a container window) is open it opens the System context menu (Save / Load / To Title / Quit), which stays open (run 03).
    usage: python -I tools/close.py
- **`common.py`**: Shared helpers for the tool scripts (run 12 review: fourteen copies of run(), six of walk(), eight idle-polls and about 150 fixed sleeps were spread over the scripts).
- **`convert.py`**: Feed named stacks into an installed converter's drag grid (the kiln's Bake, the spinner's Spin; run 28). A converter turns the WHOLE dragged stack, one piece per tick, as one AI_UseCrafter task (run 25: 124 fibers on the spinner ran SP 51 -> -19, the death by overwork): so each stack is checked against SP first (SP_EACH a piece, plus the reserve), fed one at a time, and waited out before the next. The bridge's stamina floor (0.32.0) still cancels the task at SP 3. The grid closes at the end.
    usage: python -I tools/convert.py DX DZ ACT [--sp-each N] [--max N] STACK [STACK ...]
           python -I tools/convert.py --tool "butcher's tool" [--max N] STACK [STACK ...]
      --max N  feed a bigger stack but stop after about N pieces: the bridge's stamina floor (spguard) is set
               to SP - N x sp-each for the task and put back to 3 after (run 28: 10 threads from 73 fibers)
      --tool NAME  a converter carried in the pack, opened by its Use (G65: the butcher's tool turns skins into
               2-3 hide fibers each, ~1 SP a skin, fact #1421)
      e.g. python -I tools/convert.py -1 1 Bake "6 pine logs" "5 palulu logs"     (kiln: log -> carbon log)
           python -I tools/convert.py -1 1 Spin --sp-each 1 "8 pieces of hide fiber"
      STACK  the pack stack's full name (whole-word matching; two candidates is a refusal)
    Exit 0 all fed, 1 refused (no such act, a stack missing or over the SP), 3 stopped (a hostile, a window).
- **`cookdishes.py`**: Cook the residents' dishes from the farm's fresh food (run 18, backlog P15): residents eat only prepared food from shared boxes, about 8 dishes a day while I'm home (fact #671).
    usage: python -I tools/cookdishes.py [MAX_DISHES=10] [min_sp=20]
- **`craft.py`**: Craft a recipe at a station next to the player (or with Quick Craft).
    usage: python -I tools/craft.py STATION_DX STATION_DZ "Recipe name" [count] [--dry] [--use MATERIAL] [--force]
           python -I tools/craft.py quick "Recipe name" [count] [--dry] [--use MATERIAL] [--force]
      --use rosewood  pick the "rosewood ..." stack in every ingredient slot that offers one (the
                      screen picks a default; a slot takes a single stack, so mixed woods don't add up)
      --use rosewood,voynich  several materials: each slot takes the first one it offers (run 12:
                      a bookshelf's book slots took scrolls, which count as books)
      --force         craft although SP - Stamina Cost x count would end under SP_RESERVE (errors.csv
                      row 15: four arrow batches at SP 19 drove SP to -2)
    Refuses (exit 1): a window open, no such recipe, --use matching nothing, the +1 or Craft button
    not offered (ingredients short), the SP reserve. Stops (exit 3) mid-batch at Overweight (burden
    phase 3: crafted furniture lands in the pack; run 14 ended Squashed).
- **`craftcycle.py`**: Train Blacksmith and Carpentry to their targets at home (run 42, G48 M2): repeats a cheap recipe on plentiful materials, eats, sleeps, again. Measured at Blacksmith 4, potential 242: Bolt (1 scrap, 2 SP) pays 12 exp a SP; at Carpentry 6, potential 300: the sawmill (a log, 1 SP) pays 18 exp a SP; then desks (4 planks, 3 SP, ~10 exp a SP at 8). Every step has home_guard's stops (run 41) and a failed meal is a stop.
    usage: python -I tools/craftcycle.py [--blacksmith N] [--carpentry N] [--cycles N] [--floor SP]   defaults 8, 12, 12 cycles, floor 12
    Exit 0 targets reached or the cycles run, 3 stopped (a hostile above my level, HP, hunger with no meal, materials out, a tool's stop).
- **`craftrun.py`**: A list of crafts at home's stations (run 42, G48: 30 first crafts): walks beside each station, checks the stamina, crafts one, and carries what it made to the shipping chest, or to the yard's wagon when the chest is full, before the next, since crafted furniture Squashes (a locker 56 weight, run 42). Every step goes through farmday.home_guard (run 41).
    usage: python -I tools/craftrun.py [--min-sp N] [--keep] [--ship] STATION:RECIPE[:USE] ...
           python -I tools/craftrun.py --min-sp 15 "blacksmith's table:Pipe" "mason's table:Sink:granite"
      --min-sp N  stop before a craft that would leave SP under N (default 12)
      --keep      leave what's made in the pack (materials, parts)
    Prints each craft's SP, new items and the skill exp it paid. Exit 0 all done, 1 refused (no such station), 3 stopped (SP, a refused craft, a hostile through home_guard).

- **`delve.py`**: Work through a dungeon floor with the run 04 rules (elin-play: HP decides, not the count): explore, and when a hostile shows up, fight it if it is at or below my level, loot, go on. Hands control back as soon as a decision is mine, with exit 3 and a "stop: ..." line (the review of 2026-10-23: every decision stop used to exit 0 and ladder.py parsed the text): - my HP under 70% (THRESHOLDS dungeon_hp: drink, or teleport if still under 50%) - Kaberg under 50% (heal.py) or not in the party - a hostile above my level, or 3+ at or above it in view (weak crowds are fine) - a swarm: 6+ hostiles in view, or 4+ with one at or above my level (THRESHOLDS swarm) - a window or dialog, blindness, a task still running, Hungry, Overweight (common.ready) - fight.py, shoot.py or throw.py stopping (rc 3) or refusing (rc 1) Exit 0 with its own line for the floor's natural ends: "stop: stairs found", "stop: floor explored", "stop: step limit". After one of those the corpses are butchered and the floor looted (butcher_when_safe); after a refused floor or a decision stop nothing is looted (run 17: loot.py walked an underwater floor the gate had refused). Never rests or waits (the user's rule: no idling in a dungeon).

      --solo  Kaberg stays home (run 04: she runs ahead into the dark and falls; solo at danger 2
              I take almost nothing with PV 27 and Taunt): don't stop for her absence
      --expendable  an ally along as a meat shield (the user, run 16: "if they die they just come back
              in a week"; Zone.Revive brings a dead member home within 0-7 days): her HP and her death
              don't stop the delve. Turn on the Strategy tab's "Always stay by you while in combat"
              (dontWander) first, and remember a scroll of teleport leaves her behind.
      --max-danger N / --force  the floor gate (MAX_DANGER, the thresholds table's max_danger)
      --breathe  an underwater floor, only with water breathing in hand (the user, run 17)
    Targets come from tools/threat.py (the user, run 16: casters and high damage first, high defense
    last): a kind in its "avoid" group within 8 levels of mine (4 until run 17) stops the delve instead of a melee.

A specialized book gives 1,000 skill exp (blessed 1,500, cursed 500), or teaches the skill when it is unknown (fact #554), and character exp comes only from skill level-ups (fact #481), so a book is exp sitting in a box: run 40 found ~30, filed in the library since run 27 because only an unlearned skill's book was ever read. This takes them box by box, reads each until it crumbles, and prints what each paid.

The mined walls drop on the ground: pick them up afterwards (loot.py, or ship them).

They have their own count, S1, S2 and on, and never join the kept game's run numbers, metrics or tracker (the user, same day). A game's records live in runs/ and knowledge/, and the tools read them there, so the kept game's records are parked in archive/NAME/ with a checksum of every file, and the trials get blank ones. Its save is never loaded: new characters take the game's next free world_N. The trial's floor gate and route limit go in runs/thresholds.json (gitignored, read by common.py), so no tracked file changes and the numbers leave with the records.
    usage: python -I tools/trial.py park [--yes]          show or do the parking (a second park is refused)
           python -I tools/trial.py start S8 "CHARACTER" WORLD    start a trial's clock: minutes count from here
           python -I tools/trial.py mark "LABEL" [--note TEXT]    a milestone at the current minute, in runs/milestones.csv
           python -I tools/trial.py sample [--every 20] [--max 125]  log the state every N seconds until the window or the game ends;
                                                                     a level-up marks itself. Run it in the background
           python -I tools/trial.py table                 minutes to each level and the totals, per trial, against the baselines
           python -I tools/trial.py status                what is parked and which trial is running
           python -I tools/trial.py restore [--yes]       the trials' records to archive/start-runs-DATE/, the kept game's back, every
                                                          checksum verified (exit 1 and nothing more removed if one differs)
    Exit: 0 done (or shown), 1 refused, 2 the bridge.
- **`tunnel.py`**: Mine a way through when a floor looks closed (the user, run 42: "looks like you may be stuck in the dirt, may need to mine to get a path"; one soil block at 14,15 of Boring Cave B4 held 17 real minutes and a game day and a half of "delve: step limit"). Reads the explored cells, floods from me over open ground, and finds the cheapest run of walls to open ground I can't reach (the magic map shows plenty); with none known, to the nearest unexplored cell. Then it holds the pickaxe and mines that run, nearest wall first.
    usage: python -I tools/tunnel.py [--max N=6] [--dry]    at most N walls; --dry prints the plan
           python -I tools/tunnel.py --to X,Z [--max N=8]   dig the cheapest way to that cell, through unexplored cells too (run 43: Traditional Cave B4's stairs lay
                                                            magic-mapped in a closed room, one soil block and a dark cell from the corridor, and stopped a circuit)
    Exit 0 dug (or "nothing to dig": no wall leads anywhere), 1 refused (no pickaxe, a window), 3 stopped (a hostile, a wall too hard, SP).
- **`unlock.py`**: Open a locked chest in the pack (run 42: treasure-map chests can come locked, "a cool mystic treasure chest" at lock 21; a locked chest lists as empty, and digmap.py and chests.py --field took that for empty: one was dropped on a field with its contents inside). The game's Open starts a timed task, and the next command cancels it ("You give up opening"), so each try waits for the task to end. A failed try costs no charge and no item without a lockpick; it can be tried again.
    usage: python -I tools/unlock.py [NAME] [TRIES=8]    NAME: part of the chest's name (default: the first locked chest in the pack)
    Exit 0 opened (or none locked), 1 refused (no such chest), 3 stopped (still locked after TRIES, a hostile, a window).
- **`unpack.py`**: Open the mail: every package (delivery box) on the map, one at a time, with its contents listed. Deliveries, quest rewards and the tax bill arrive in packages by the hearth or the mail post, and they pile up unopened (run 04 found four, holding a tool, a can, a bottle).
    usage: python -I tools/unpack.py [--take] [--pickup] [radius]
    Then triage what came out (elin-play: use now / bring / store / sell or ship).
- **`valuables.py`**: List the furniture installed on this map with its base value and weight, most valuable first (the user, run 08: dungeon wall lights are worth money). Dungeon and nefia furniture belongs to nobody: take it with a right-click Grab (`act.py DX DZ "Grab (a wall light" right`; pick up what lies on top first), then `hotbar.py --deselect` to put it in the pack. In towns it is someone's property (theft: Karma -1): this tool says so and lists nothing there.
    usage: python -I tools/valuables.py [min_value=500] [max_weight=15]
           python -I tools/valuables.py --take NAME [MAX=14]   grab every installed NAME on this map
      (run 16: 15 wall lights in a nefia shipped for 67 each). Stops (exit 3) on a hostile in view
      (fight, then run it again) and when the pack gets heavy (speed matters: drop heavy loot by the
      stairs, finish the floor, pick it up after).
- **`view.py`**: Look at a spot of the map from a fixed vantage cell: walk there, capture the Elin window (PrintWindow, window-only), crop around the target cell and save it zoomed. Captures stay in runs/captures/ (gitignored).
    usage: python -I tools/view.py VX,VZ TX,TZ [name] [--back]
      VX,VZ  vantage cell to stand on (walls near the player render cut away)
      TX,TZ  map cell to center the crop on
      --back walk back to where you started afterwards
- **`wade.py`**: Leave an ambush map through shallow water: step toward an edge one cell at a time and take its Enter.
    usage: python -I tools/wade.py [DIR=nearest|w|e|n|s] [MAX_STEPS=20]
    Exit 0 when it left the map, 3 stopped for a decision (hostile, deep water ahead, HP lost, blocked).
- **`wait.py`**: Pass game time safely until a clock time: the bed's Pass Time when standing on a bed, otherwise repeated Wait. Cancels (bridge `cancel`) at the target time or on any threat: a hostile in view, HP below 80%, worse than plain Hungry, or a dialog/window opening. Run 03 lesson: an unwatched Pass Time ran 21 game hours and a resident died meanwhile.
    usage: python -I tools/wait.py HH:MM --user-ok   only with the user's yes for this wait
    The user (runs 05, 11, 17): "Please don't wait... Waiting is the worst thing we can do in this
    game as it costs hunger/time with no benefit." Run 17 waited 3.5 game hours for a shop to open;
    so it refuses without --user-ok: do SP-free work, travel or sleep instead.
- **`wait_ingame.py`**: Wait until Elin is running with a game loaded (after a launch with autoload), then print the bridge version and a compact look. Exits 1 on timeout.
    usage: python -I tools/wait_ingame.py [timeout_seconds]
- **`wallmine.py`**: Mine the dungeon walls around me with the pickaxe (run 14): a Machinarium's metal frames give a scrap each (the blacksmith's table's binding material since run 05) for about 1 SP, and every wall trains Mining (G11 wants Mining 10: the basalt pickaxe then opens the home's iron big rock).
    usage: python -I tools/wallmine.py [N=20] [min_sp=10] [radius=6] [--kind metal]
    Scans the cells within RADIUS for walls/blocks whose right-click offers "Collect", nearest first,
    and harvests up to N of them (harvest.py: walks there, collects, picks up the drop). Stops (exit 3)
    on a hostile in view, SP under the floor, a window, or a full pack; exit 0 when no wall is left;
    exit 1 without a pickaxe. --kind keeps only blocks whose name has KIND. (minewalls.py is the
    home practice loop; this one mines dungeon walls.)
- **`watchlog.py`**: Follow a log with a stop condition: the only way to watch a log here (2026-11-03, KB #155).
    usage: python -I tools/watchlog.py LOG [--match RE] [--until RE] [--max SECONDS=1790] [--idle SECONDS=900] [--from-start]
      --match RE     print only the lines that match (default: every line)
      --until RE     print the first line that matches and exit 0
      --max SECONDS  exit 3 after this long (never over 3600)
      --idle SECONDS say so once when the log hasn't grown for this long: silence isn't success
      --from-start   read what the log already holds (default: only what is added from now on)
    exit codes: 0 --until matched, 1 refused (bad arguments), 3 the deadline passed: re-arm if it is still needed.
- **`water.py`**: Water the home field once (run 10): take the can from its box if needed, refill it at the lake when it holds fewer charges than the field has cells (TaskWater spends one charge a cell), "Water crops", and put the can back in the tool box. Water after 06:00: the next morning's growth tick is doubled (+10 instead of +5) on watered cells, and the flag clears after each tick.
    usage: python -I tools/water.py [--keep] [--extra X,Z [X,Z ...]]   (--keep leaves the can in the pack)
    The field is farmday.FIELD.
- **`wgo.py`**: World-map travel with the game's own pathing (the user's tip, run 08: clicking a place walks there around cliffs). Sends AI_Goto to the named place's cell, polls until I arrive, land on a local map (an ambush), see a hostile within 4, or HP drops under 60%; then cancels the walk so it doesn't resume after an ambush (run 08: a leftover goto walked me 14 game hours further).
    usage: python -I tools/wgo.py NAME [--weak-ok] [--ambush]   a place from `bridge.py places` (name or id)
           python -I tools/wgo.py X Z [--weak-ok] [--ambush]    an absolute world-map cell
      --near N   stop for a hostile within N cells (default 4)
      --walk-ok  walk home although it is over 10 tiles away (run 49: refused otherwise: a return scroll is ~15 turns)
      --weak-ok  keep walking past hostiles 3+ levels below me (a lone crab kept stopping the walk;
                 if one ambushes, the fight is easy); anything stronger still stops it
      --ambush   handle an ambush map instead of handing back (the review of 2026-10-23: travel was the
                 largest real-time sink and every ambush stopped the tool): the swarm rule and the
                 level rule of elin-play's table, then fight.py one foe at a time (nearest first),
                 loot.py 20, purge.py --free 3 (run 35), leave.py, and the walk goes on. Anything the rules refuse stops (exit 3).
    NAME: an exact name or id wins; else a part of the name, which must fit one place name only
    (several places of that one name: the nearest); two or more different names refuse (exit 1, the
    way common.pick does). Refuses off the world map (zone.region, bridge 0.30.0) and for an
    underwater dungeon without --breathe. Exit 0 on arrival; exit 3 (stop) on an ambush (a local
    map: look.py), a hostile close, HP under 60%, a window, hunger or SP, or when not moving.
    Every leg is logged (the user, run 12: travel time belongs in the graph): a row in
    knowledge/travel.csv and, for a leg of 3+ steps, a `kb.py add` fact with the game hours, the
    steps walked and how it ended. Run 12 measured about 2.5-3 game hours a world-map step.
- **`whereis.py`**: Ask a town guard "Where is..." and let the game walk me there (AI_Goto), then wait until I've arrived. Picks the guard's entry by text, never by index.
    usage: python -I tools/whereis.py GUARD|any TARGET
      e.g. python -I tools/whereis.py Elfeus "furniture shopkeeper"
           python -I tools/whereis.py Elfeus "tax chest"
    Refuses (exit 1) standing in deep water (pc.inWater, bridge 0.30.0), without a guard or an entry;
    stops (exit 3) when the sweep or the guard's walk heads into deep water (run 19's drowning).
- **`woodrun.py`**: Cut wood on a field map for a craft push (run 42, G48: Carpentry needs about 70 logs at potential 145; a forest tile beside home gives a log and two branches a tree, 0.5 SP, about 9 real seconds; the map is fog until walked, so it alternates gather.py and explore.py). Logs go into the haul bag, where purge can't drop them; branches past the cap are dropped.
    usage: python -I tools/woodrun.py LOGS [--minutes M=8] [--min-sp 30]
    Stops at LOGS held in all (pack and bags), the time, SP under the floor, Hungry (a meal first, a failed meal is a stop), or a hostile it can't fight (common.ready's reasons).
    Exit 0 target or time reached, 1 refused (not on a field map, no axe), 3 stopped.
- **`wrecks.py`**: Mine every wreck on the explored map with the pickaxe and pick up what drops (run 06: five wrecks on one floor of Spiritual Cave; wrecks give gems, scrap, fiber, bolts, logs).
    usage: python -I tools/wrecks.py [R=60] [min_hp_pct=70] [min_sp=5]
- **`yardchests.py`**: Bring in the treasure chests lying loose on the home map (run 43: seven from Poppy's Treasure Hunt lay in the yard, about 2,000 orens, 3 bars and 2 medals each; elin-home said arrive.py picked them up, and no tool did). One at a time, on its own cell: item.py takes the first of a name, and a locked twin in the pack stops chests.py (run 42). A locked one goes through unlock.py in the pack (a loose chest has no Pick Lock act) and back on its cell if it won't open.
    usage: python -I tools/yardchests.py [--dry]     --dry lists them with their locks and moves nothing
    Exit 0 done (or none), 1 refused (not at home), 3 stopped (home_guard's stops, chests.py's stop).
- **`zap.py`**: Zap a carried rod on myself N times (run 14: Magic Device, a new skill, levels with every zap). Only rods that are harmless on oneself: holy shield, holy light, cure ..., keeping KEEP charges.
    usage: python -I tools/zap.py "rod of holy shield" [N=5] [--keep K=3]
    Opens the backpack (where the rods ride), holds the fullest stack of the rod (common.grab, a
    whole-word match), right-click Zap on my own cell, repeats; stops (exit 3) on a hostile in view or
    a window; ends (exit 0) with the rod down to K charges. Prints skill-up lines.
